title: Treatment planning
description: A written plan first: options, sequence, timeline, and reference costs so you can decide without pressure. If anything unexpected comes up, I discuss it with you before continuing.
highlights: Review or update plan at any stage

items.name: Initial consultation + written plan
items.description: Clinical exam, diagnostic discussion, and a written treatment plan with options, timeline, and reference prices.

items.name: Complex multi-phase planning
items.description: Comprehensive plan for full-mouth rehabilitation, implants, or extensive restorative work. Includes phased timeline and specialist referrals if needed.

items.name: Plan update / second revision
items.description: If your situation has changed or you want a different approach, I update the plan with new options. Existing patients only.

process: Comprehensive clinical exam and records review
Diagnostic tests if needed (x-rays, photos, models)
I draft a written plan with options and costs
We review together — you ask questions, I clarify
You decide when to start, in which phase, and how

faqs.q: Do I have to commit to the plan?
faqs.a: No. The plan is yours to consider. You decide when — or whether — to start treatment. There's no obligation.
Yes. If something unexpected comes up during treatment, I discuss it with you before continuing. The plan is a starting point, not a contract.

faqs.q: Is the written plan included in the consultation?
faqs.a: Yes. The initial consultation fee includes the exam, the diagnosis discussion, and the written plan with options.

faqs.q: Can I share the plan with another dentist?
faqs.a: Absolutely. The plan is yours. Many patients share it with their regular dentist or use it to get a second opinion from a specialist.
